root_cause.text: The MPRLS0025PA SPI driver in `drivers/iio/pressure/mprls0025pa_spi.c` used an uninitialized `struct spi_transfer` on the stack, so stale garbage fields could be passed to the SPI core during `mpr_spi_xfer()`, causing incorrect transfer setup and undefined behavior.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `struct spi_transfer xfer;` to `struct spi_transfer xfer = { };` and the commit message explicitly says “Make sure that the spi_transfer struct is zeroed out before use,” indicating the bug was failure to initialize the transfer structure in the SPI driver.

intent_record.intent_summary: Zero-initialize the SPI transfer structure to avoid using uninitialized fields during SPI transfers.
intent_record.what: The local variable `struct spi_transfer xfer` in `mpr_spi_xfer()` was changed from an uninitialized automatic variable to a zero-initialized variable using `= { }`.
intent_record.how: This ensures all fields in the SPI transfer structure start as zero instead of containing indeterminate stack data, preventing unintended behavior from uninitialized members when the transfer is used.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in `mpr_spi_xfer()`: it declares `struct spi_transfer xfer;` and then only assigns `xfer.tx_buf`, `xfer.rx_buf`, and `xfer.len` before calling `spi_sync_transfer(spi, &xfer, 1);`. There is no initialization of the whole struct (for example no `memset`, no `{}` initializer, and no `SPI_TRANSFER_INITIALIZER`), so stale stack garbage fields could be passed to the SPI core. The fix is not present in this snippet because the transfer object remains uninitialized apart from those three fields.
